The task contract shows four sampled candidates, all successful; the best score is `solver_7ef7a2606ab6` and the three prefill-equivalent runs tie below it. I’m now anchoring the visuals to the inherited guidance, observations, metrics, diagnostics, and optimizer notes; if there is no sampled failure, I’ll explicitly use the most informative lower-scoring success as the comparator.

The sampled metrics isolate one clean change: raising `tail_steering_gain` from `0.60` to `0.65` improves arrival by `1.70` time units and mean distance by `0.0162L`, with slightly lower total command energy but modestly higher crossflow/load. The current `0.60` prefill is exactly reproduced in three runs, so this is deterministic same-prewarm evidence rather than sampling noise; I’m checking whether the keyframes support a tighter route rather than a visually unstable shortcut.

The assigned parent’s unevaluated midpoint hypothesis is now evaluated and negative: static `oscillator_energy_gain=2.075` reached in `77.26`, raised mean distance to `2.551L`, energy to `53,643`, and force/moment to `31.45/454.27`, all worse than static `2.1`. I’m treating that as the most informative failed optimization comparator and will fold it into the existing non-monotone restoration lesson; it argues against combining the tail-share gain with another restoration interpolation.

The visual diagnosis and falsifiable hypothesis are now recorded before the policy edit, as the skill requires. The candidate will make one controlled change only: `tail_steering_gain=0.70`, an equal `0.05` continuation beyond the evaluated `0.65` improvement, while retaining static restoration `2.1` and every other anchor parameter.

The first guidance patch did not apply because the inherited paragraph wraps differently than the excerpt I anchored against; no file was changed by that failed patch.
